summary: Xianda works in Buddhist studies. He earned a BA from the University of Kelaniya and a PhD from the University of Hong Kong by 2016, studying under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti and teacher Toshiichi Endo.

Xiangguang Zhou worked in Sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies, studying under Swami Sivananda Saraswati. He held posts at the University of Delhi, University of Allahabad, Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration, and Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy around 1960.

Xianlin Ji worked in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Shandong University, Tsinghua University, and the University of Göttingen (PhD 1935–1945) under Ernst Waldschmidt and Emil Sieg, later holding leadership and professorial posts at Peking University, CASS, and CAS.

Xiaoling Wu specialized in Sinology and Indology. He held academic posts at Visva-Bharati University (~1942–1947), Peking University, Academia Sinica (~1950–1977), and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–1995).
Xiaoting Wei works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Kathy Ku Cheng Mei, attested in 2004.
Xinchuan Huang was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University (~1952–1958) and served as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978).

Xinru Liu specializes in Indology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania (~1980–1985) under Ludo Rocher and held professorships at CASS (1993) and The College of New Jersey (~2002–2021).
Xiuzhi Zeng works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Zeng completed an MA at Nanhua University under supervisor Meihua Chen, attested in 2006.

Xu Dishan worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, having studied at Yenching University, Columbia University, and the University of Oxford. He later held posts at Peking University (~1926–1935), Tsinghua University (~1927–1935), and the University of Hong Kong (~1935–1941).

Xuesong Zhang works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He earned a PhD from The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xueyu (attested 2008) and served as an associate professor at Renmin University of China (attested 2015).

Xuezhu Li works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, and studied under Shoryu Katsura. He served as a Research Associate at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2010–2022) and was a Numata fellow at Ryukoku University in 2011.

Y. Karunadasa worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying at the University of Ceylon and earning a PhD at the University of London under David Friedman. He held posts at the University of Kelaniya, PGIPBS, HKU, SOAS, Calgary, and Toronto.

Yael Bentor works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Indiana University under Gregory Schopen, David Shulman, and others, and later taught Indian Studies at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (attested 1995–2000).

Yamada Koun was a religious studies and Buddhist studies figure who studied at the First Higher School and the University of Tokyo. He trained under several Zen masters, founded Kamakura Haku-un-kai (1953), and became head of Sanbo Zen in 1970.
Yanfei Zhou works in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Sinology. Zhou completed a PhD at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet-Keung Lo.

Yang Renshan was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He founded the Jinling Scriptural Press (1897) and Jetavana Hermitage (1908), and founded and headed the Buddhist Research Society in 1910.
Yang-Gyu An works in Buddhist studies. He earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford by 1998 under Richard Gombrich and also studied under Hojin.
Yangdon Dhondup is a scholar in Tibetology. She completed her PhD at SOAS University of London (~2000–2004) under the supervision of Henry Y. H. Zhao.

Yanling Chen works in Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi and also studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun (attested 2012).
Yanpei was active in Buddhist studies. He studied under Taixu (~1934–1947) and under Yin Shun (~1941–1952).
